en: Fine-tuning is in the end the post-training
part of an AI model. It's that part where
a raw foundation model, as it's also called,
the model you get out of pre-training, is
turned into a useful assistant, for example.
It's also fine-tuning you could perform if
you have the hardware for it and if you have
a model that kind of supports it to build on
top of a small language model, for example,
to optimize it for your specific tasks.
The idea behind fine-tuning is that you take
a finished model
and then you generate more data and you use
a fine-tuning tool. There are various tools
out there you can use to produce an updated
version of the model, you could say, based
on what it already was able to do combined
with your new data where your new data gets
a higher priority to kind of nudge the model
into a certain direction. That can be a
certain writing style you want to teach the
model. It can be a certain behavior that it
ends every question with, yes, sir, if you
want to, or anything like that, or that it
has certain knowledge it might otherwise not
have. And fine-tuning, therefore, is a vital
process that is performed by all these large
AI labs. When they finish up their new
models before they release them to the
public, but that can also be done by you or
your company to build your own very specific
models that are great at specific tasks.
